subject: Request: Article 30 processing register export, DPIA artifacts & KMS rotation proof
messages:
From: Emma Hughes <emma.hughes@novabank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@novabank.com>; compliance_ops@novabank.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: Article 30 processing register export, DPIA artifacts & KMS rotation proof

Hi Olga,

Hope you’re well. As part of an internal audit ahead of our QA committee next month, Legal and Compliance are requesting the following from Redwood for our account: NovaBank (contract ref NB-2024-78):

- A machine-readable export (CSV/Excel) of the Article 30 processing activities register that covers all processing attributable to NovaBank (data categories, processing purposes, recipients/subprocessors, transfers, retention).
- A short DPIA artifacts pack or summary that shows the DPIA decision, risk mitigations relevant to automated inference features, and any recent re-evaluations.
- Evidence of the most recent KMS key rotation and the rotation schedule (audit summary or rotation log).
- Clarification on cross-border transfers and the legal basis for transfers to any non-EU subprocessors (if applicable).

Can we get this by 2026-11-10? If some items require a confidentiality or access agreement, please advise the fastest way to obtain it — we can route through our GRC portal.

Thanks in advance,
Emma Hughes
Head of Vendor Risk — NovaBank
emma.hughes@novabank.com
+44 20 7123 4567

---
Attachments requested: list of required artifacts (see above)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Hughes <emma.hughes@novabank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:04:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Request: Article 30 processing register export, DPIA artifacts & KMS rotation proof

Emma — thanks for the clear ask. We can provide everything you listed; below is a proposed delivery plan so we align on scope and access: 

1) Article 30 register export (CSV): we will export the processing activities that map specifically to the NovaBank account identifier in our tenancy. That file will include processing purpose, categories of personal data, third-party subprocessors, transfers, and retention periods.
2) DPIA artifacts: we will prepare a 2–3 page summary plus the DPIA extract showing mitigations for automated inference and any residual risk assessments relevant to your use cases.
3) KMS rotation evidence: we can provide the rotation log summary (dates, key IDs, rotation type) and an internal attestation doc.
4) Cross-border transfers: we will include the current subprocessor inventory (highlighting non-EU subprocessors) and the legal mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, or other).

Quick clarifying Qs: 
- Do you need the register in English only or also with mapping to your internal data asset names?
- Is a time-limited Drive link fine for the artifacts, or do you require SFTP/secure share?

Our plan and ETA: internal prep today/tomorrow; target delivery (secure link + attachments) 2026-11-05 EOD if no additional legal gating is required. If NovaBank needs an NDA or a specific recipient signature, we’ll pause until we receive that.

Looping in Marcus (security) and Karthik (privacy) to confirm the KMS export and DPIA excerpt.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Privacy & Policy Manager
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0192
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:22:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Request: Article 30 processing register export, DPIA artifacts & KMS rotation proof

Olga — I ran the export and attached the initial artifacts below for internal review. Notes: 
- Attached CSV (processing_register_export_olga_20261104.csv) contains row-level flags so we can easily filter to NovaBank account id NB-2024-78. I redacted internal-only operator notes.
- KMS rotation summary attached (kms-rotation-summary-2026.pdf). This shows the rotation on 2026-09-21 and the scheduled rotation policy.
- DPIA excerpt is a redacted 2-page summary for external consumption.

I recommend we: (a) let Legal/Compliance request a time-limited link, and (b) provide a brief cover note describing redactions and the scope. I will prepare the rotation attestation if needed.

Attachments (internal review): processing_register_export_olga_20261104.csv; kms-rotation-summary-2026.pdf; dpia-summary-novabank-excerpt.pdf

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
From: Emma Hughes <emma.hughes@novabank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@novabank.com>; compliance_ops@novabank.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 10:31:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Request: Article 30 processing register export, DPIA artifacts & KMS rotation proof

Thanks Olga and Marcus — that sounds good. A few follow-ups from Legal: 

- Please confirm whether NimbusCloud (nimbuscloud.com) is listed as a subprocessor used for inference serving and, if so, whether transfers to NimbusCloud rely on SCCs or adequacy.
- We would prefer a time-limited Drive link (with view-only and download disabled) for the initial delivery, followed by an SFTP transfer for any CSV extracts if necessary.
- For the Article 30 register, please include the column headers and a short README explaining any internal codes (e.g., processing purpose codes).

If you can provide the Drive link and the small DPIA summary by 2026-11-08 EOD that would be ideal; we can escalate to a live review call if questions remain.

Regards,
Emma
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:45:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Request: Article 30 processing register export, DPIA artifacts & KMS rotation proof

Emma — attaching the temporary Drive link and the requested artifacts. Summary of what's included: 

- redwood_article30_register_2026.csv — Article 30 export filtered to NovaBank account id NB-2024-78; column headers are documented in README.txt within the folder.
- dpia-summary-novabank-excerpt.pdf — 2-page externally-redacted DPIA summary (automated inference mitigations highlighted).
- kms-rotation-summary-2026.pdf — rotation history and attestation draft.

Subprocessors: NimbusCloud is listed as a caching/edge provider for EU regions and the transfer is covered by SCCs (standard contractual clauses). The full subprocessor inventory in the folder highlights this and the legal mechanism.

Drive link (time-limited, view only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4dRedwoodArticle30Export (access expires 2026-11-23)

If you would like us to push the CSV to your SFTP, please share host/creds in the secure portal or tell us the contact for file delivery. We can set up a 30-minute review call tomorrow morning CET to walk through the artifacts if helpful.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Privacy & Policy Manager
Redwood Inference
